rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Convection** transfers heat by the bulk motion of the fluid itself: heated fluid expands, loses density, rises by buoyancy, and cooler fluid sinks to replace it — a **convection current**. Natural convection is buoyancy-driven (sea breeze, boiling, chimney draught); forced convection uses pumps and fans (radiators, blood flow).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Buoyancy: warm fluid density ρ_T = ρ₀(1−γΔT) - Heat carried: dQ/dt = ṁcΔT (mass flow rate ṁ)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Convection moves matter, conduction moves only energy.**  ·  **"Radiators" in rooms mostly convect** — the name is a misnomer.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Heat That Rides the Current Convection moves heat by moving matter itself: warmed fluid expands, becomes lighter, and rises while cooler fluid sinks to replace it. The loop powers boiling pots, sea breezes, room heaters and monsoons — and it cannot exist in a solid or in free fall.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2024) ### 2.1 Definition and mechanism **Convection** is the transfer of heat by the **actual motion (bulk flow) of the heated material** — possible only in fluids. Heated fluid expands (density falls), buoyancy lifts it, and denser cooler fluid takes its place, setting up a **convection current**.…

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short (2m): Why are room-heater outlets placed near the floor and AC outlets near the ceiling?** — Warm air rises (heater at floor drives the convection loop through the room); cool air sinks (AC at ceiling lets it fall), so both positionings exploit natural convection.

rows.text: Sea breeze and freezer-position explanations are the classic 2–3m follow-ups.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Convection stops in microgravity — ISS flames are spherical; boiling behaves entirely differently.
